CIRCUIT: a linear power supply. 100 V / 1 kHz AC source -> full-wave bridge (D#2/D#0 upper, D#12/D#13 lower) -> C#5 100 uF and L#9 1 uH in series across the rails as the filter leg -> a 1 kohm resistor and a 10 V zener set the reference on the base of PNP Q#7, whose collector drives the op-amp's + input; the op-amp output drives series-pass NPN Q#3 (collector on the raw rail), whose emitter feeds the output through L#8 1 uH into the L#8/R#14 node, and a 5 V zener returns that node to the op-amp's - input. 16 components, 12 nets. NOTE: the sheet has no GND symbol, so no net is named '0'; the bottom rail (n11) is the common return.

JUDGEMENT CALLS:
  S9 (175,514) -> CROSSING, overriding the tracer's default junction. At 12x this is an unmistakable semicircular hop: the horizontal wire coming from the AC source's bottom terminal rises into a clean half-circle over the left bridge column (x~175) and drops back to y~525 on the far side, then runs on to S13. The junction reading is what the tracer produced, and it is electrically impossible: it tied both terminals of the AC source to the same net (the summary shows 6.0 and 6.1 both on n2), i.e. it short-circuited the source and collapsed the bridge's two AC nodes into one. Rule 1 settles it even without the ink.
  S13 (259,524) -> JUNCTION. A fat solder blob (dot=2.1, clearly wider than the strokes in both axes) where that same source wire lands on the right bridge column. This pair is the drafter's own habit demonstrated on one wire: hop where he means 'not connected', dot where he means 'connected'.
  S7 (176,446) -> JUNCTION. Plain T: the source's top lead ends on the left column, which continues above and below. No crossing reading exists.
  S0 (527,351), S1 (358,353), S2 (246,354) -> JUNCTION. Ts where the 1 kohm leg, the 100 uF leg and the D#0 column drop off the top rail.
  S12 (535,520) -> JUNCTION. T where the branch to the base of PNP #7 leaves the R#1/Z#10 column.
  S27 (538,657), S28 (623,659, became critical once C#15's bottom lead was retargeted to its real port), S29 (266,661), S30 (374,660) -> JUNCTION. Ts where the 10 V zener, the 10 uF capacitor, D#13 and L#9 land on the bottom rail.
  Non-critical sites left at default, none of which changes the netlist: S11/S14/S16/S17 (the '100V 1KHz' caption riding on the source's bottom wire - all fragments are on that one wire), S18/S19/S20 (the '1 uH' captions), S21/S22/S24 (the '5 V' and '10 uF' captions on Z#11's leads), S23/S25/S26 (the '10 kohm' caption on R#14 - checked specifically that this caption does not bridge R#14's top node n10 to the bottom rail; it does not), and S8, the op-amp's own inverting-input stub.
